snippet.title: The Italian Trump: Who Are the Voters of Anger?
snippet.description:
A fascinating political and social plunge into the heart of an Italy in full metamorphosis and a 2,000-kilometer journey across the peninsula to understand how a single man caused Italy to tip into anti-migrant populism. In the space of a single year, Matteo Salvini completely upended the European political chessboard by propelling the League from 17% to 30% in voting intentions, while blocking the arrival of migrants on Italian shores and openly defying leaders in Paris and Berlin.
Director: Antoine Robin

ABOUT IT:

Nicknamed "the Italian Trump" by his fiercest opponents, this ally of Marine Le Pen fascinates as much as he worries with his nationalist leanings and verbal excesses. Yet, behind the media discourse lies a massive electoral reality, marked by 78% of Italians supporting his strict security policy. Director Antoine Robin embarked on a 2,000-kilometer sociological road movie, from the north to the south of the peninsula, to meet this silent majority that is never heard.

This film gives a voice to ordinary citizens in an attempt to understand the deep reasons behind their vote, whether driven by ardent conviction or by deep spite toward the system. From bus drivers in Veneto to trade unionists and workers in Bologna, along with an entrepreneur from Verona, a lawyer from Senigallia, a professor emeritus, a farmer from Naples, or a senator from the capital in Rome, everyone reveals their intimate motivations. An unprecedented exploration on the borderline of a country weary of traditional politics, where some secretly dream of seeing a new authority figure emerge.

snippet.title: Radium Girls | Poisoned for A Paycheck (History ASMR)
snippet.description:
In the 1920s, hundreds of young women were hired to paint glowing watch dials with radium — and told the paint was harmless. It was not. This is the complete, detailed story of the Radium Girls: the forgotten workers who were slowly poisoned by their own employer, the corporate cover-up that tried to bury the truth, and the dying women who fought back and changed American law forever.
This is a full historical deep dive into one of the most important and least understood chapters in the history of labor, science, and corporate accountability. We trace the entire story from the radium craze that swept the world after Marie Curie's discovery, through the dial-painting factories of Orange, New Jersey and Ottawa, Illinois, to the courtrooms where dying women testified against the corporations that had betrayed them.
Across this documentary we cover:
— The radium craze of the early 20th century and why an entire society believed a deadly element was a miracle cure
— The dial painters known as the "Ghost Girls" and the lip-pointing technique that poisoned them
— The science of radium poisoning and why the companies protected themselves while leaving their workers exposed
— Mollie Maggia and the first horrifying deaths
— The falsified Harvard report and the corporate cover-up
— Grace Fryer and the Case of the Five Women Doomed to Die
— Catherine Donohue's deathbed testimony and the words that echoed across the nation
— How these women created the legal foundation for modern workplace safety law and OSHA
— Why their graves still register radiation nearly a century later
This is the story of Grace Fryer, Mollie Maggia, Katherine Schaub, and Catherine Donohue — real women, with real names, who deserve to be remembered not as ghosts, but as fighters.
If this story moved you, tell us in the comments: which of these women stayed with you? Say their names. Being remembered is the one form of justice they can still receive.

snippet.description:
How was England formed? In this video, we explore the fascinating history behind the creation of England — from early Celtic tribes and Roman rule to the arrival of the Anglo-Saxons and the unification of kingdoms.

After the fall of the Roman Empire in Britain, several Anglo-Saxon kingdoms such as Wessex, Mercia, and Northumbria emerged. Over time, these kingdoms competed for power until one ruler began to unite them. The process of forming England was influenced by wars, Viking invasions, cultural changes, and political alliances.

Learn how early settlers shaped the land, how kingdoms merged, and how England eventually became one unified nation. This video breaks down the key historical events that led to the birth of England and its early monarchy.

snippet.title: Why is blue one of the rarest colors in nature?
snippet.description:
Why is blue one of the rarest colors in nature? 🌍💙 In this fascinating video, we explore the science behind why blue is so uncommon in plants, animals, and natural minerals. While we see blue skies and oceans every day, truly blue pigments are surprisingly rare in the natural world. Discover how physics, light, and biology work together to create the illusion of blue in many living things.

From the wings of the Morpho butterfly to the feathers of blue birds, most “blue” colors in nature aren’t actually pigments—they’re produced by microscopic structures that bend and scatter light. Learn how structural coloration works and why evolution has made blue such a rare phenomenon in the natural world.

If you enjoy science facts, nature mysteries, and amazing discoveries about our planet, this video is for you!
